scope: Reviewed native semantic corrections identified per source annotation, not merely per issue. Several annotations may implement separate parts of one issue. The exhaustive annotation inventory tracks unlisted anchors separately; neither inventory nor an entry-level overlay proves semantic implementation.

reviews.implemented_scope: All common stream entry values and recursively contained array/dictionary values in cross-reference streams are direct; F is prohibited. Trailer Root and Encrypt references remain permitted.
Cross-reference streams cannot carry Metadata or associated files, including unknown-key extension entries in generated schemas.

A polygon/polyline Path takes precedence over Vertices. The original grid's prohibition is not enforced: accompanying Vertices are ignored, even if they are not numeric coordinates. Path validates the initial moveto and subsequent line/curve operand lengths.

PDF 2.0 choice indices are allowed without MultiSelect. Distinct display names sharing an export value require explicit indices. Effective header/catalog version validation preserves the PDF 1.7 restriction. V remains authoritative if V and I disagree.
The AP qualifier is required except for Table166 exceptions in PDF 2.0, but optional for PDF1.2–1.7. Effective page annotation graphs execute the condition; private dictionaries do not.
Rect uses zero-based array indices: the AP exception requires Rect[0]==Rect[2] AND Rect[1]==Rect[3]. A horizontal/vertical line alone remains subject to the PDF 2.0 AP requirement.
Exponential function dictionaries enforce the domain restrictions already enforced by the native builder: fractional N excludes negative x; negative N excludes zero.

PDF 2.0 embedded-file Subtype names contain a MIME type/subtype without parameters, semicolon, equals or number sign. The associated-file graph, native PDF 2.0 version gate and ISO2 schemas share the immutable media type object. PDF1.7 native first-class names remain possible.
Extensions and developer extensions schemas enforce recursively direct objects including custom entries, bounded traversal and prohibit Metadata/AF.
The linearization parameter schema enforces recursively direct objects including custom entries and prohibits Metadata/AF. The native writer constructs only managed direct parameters.

The signature schema prohibits Metadata/AF when ByteRange is present. Native pending signatures reject those entries; legitimate nested Signature Reference Data references are not recursively prohibited.

Name tree node schemas require complete, strictly byte-lexically ordered string-key/value pairs, reject direct or indirect null keys, and preserve null values. Whole-tree uniqueness and limits are separate native graph mechanisms.
Number tree node schemas require complete, strictly numerically ordered integer-key/value pairs, reject direct or indirect null keys, and preserve null values.
Structure tree root K rejects an explicit null value or null array members, including indirect null targets.
Structure element Ref rejects null members, including indirect null targets; an empty Ref array remains allowed.
Structure element K rejects explicit null and null members; integer zero remains a valid MCID.
Structure element A rejects null attribute objects and revisions; revision zero remains allowed.
Structure element C rejects null class names and revisions; revision zero remains allowed.
Null holes in ParentTree value arrays remain allowed: non-null structure-member checks do not recurse into ParentTree values.
Form XObject schemas prohibit simultaneous effective StructParent and StructParents, preserving dictionary-null-as-absence and zero keys.
Structure element access schemas prohibit simultaneous effective StructParent and StructParents.

DPM permits NameType values recursively, including indirect values, while preserving its existing string, date, array, dictionary, boolean and numeric value families.
DPM name values require valid decoded UTF-8 bytes in native construction and effective frozen/incremental graph validation. Name serialization preserves proper PDF #HH escaping.

Native FontDescriptor and PDF 2.0 schema admit integer FontWeight values from 1 through 1000 inclusive, combined with the type correction #152. Effective-version validation keeps 100-step historical PDF 1.x weights. Recommended 100-step weights are not mandatory in PDF 2.0.
Table 322 gains the missing optional boolean PV entry for cutting-plane visibility, with default true documented. This exposes typed serializable objects, not a 3D rendering engine.

Every activation Scripts reference is an indirect file specification with matching object identity in the same annotation RichMediaContent Assets name tree. Empty or absent Scripts executes nothing; no script execution is implemented. Frozen incremental graphs recheck membership.

FontWeight is an integer in the inclusive range 1..1000 when combined with #474. Native effective PDF 2.0 requires an explicit IntegerType; legacy PDF 1.x preserves accepted real-typed traditional weights.

DocMDP P is typed integer in the PDF 2.0 schema. Native DocMdpTransform creates IntegerType permission levels. Frozen raw transform dictionaries require IntegerType under effective PDF 2.0, including catalog version upgrades; historical PDF 1.x permits integral numeric objects. Missing P defaults to 2, and the domain remains 1 through 3.

GlyphOrientationVertical has PDF 2.0 type integer or name. The existing native StandardStructureAttributes domain enforces /Auto or allowed 90-degree rotations. ISO1 schema remains a separate number-or-name interpretation.

Attribute objects within each class and across ordered C classes use later-in-array precedence for repeated O or NS owners. Direct A values retain priority, including Placement used to decide LineHeight inheritance. Conflicting direct A values remain rejected.

A class absent from ClassMap resolves to an explicit empty AttributeClass without changing the serialized ClassMap. Missing or explicitly empty classes contribute no attribute and preserve ordinary inheritance and defaults.

The EmbeddedFiles name tree may contain additional attachments. The catalog AF payload must still occur in that tree, and the hidden Collection.D must select that same object, including in projected incremental graphs. The wrapper itself must remain unencrypted.
